title: Does a longer window, a lower gamma or a delay prior fix the period aliasing and early-start failures of GCC audio sync on real clips?
summary: Follow-up to capture-residgate section D. On ten real LibreOffice gallery clips (0 dB white noise, 0.8 s offset, 432 windows per clip and cell), the share of delay estimates over 2 ms off on the four failing clips falls from 97% at a 1 s window to 38% at 2 s and 16% at 3 s (gamma 0.25), because two cameras with a 0.8 s offset share only W−0.8 s of audio. Gamma moves 2 s results between 38% and 76% (PHAT worst). A tone clip (space2) is not helped by more audio (52–70% aliased at 2 and 3 s); only a delay prior tighter than its 12 ms period works (oracle ±10 ms: 0% wrong; ±50 ms: 65% still aliased). The early-start failures of untie and soft (59–77% wrong when the window starts in the clip's first half second, 0% later) are partly a short shared segment; the shared audio is only 2–5 dB quieter in wrong windows, so loudness is a weak explanation. Limits: ten clips, white noise at one SNR, 3 s windows barely vary their start (one draw of content per clip), the prior is an oracle ceiling.
lede: does a longer window or a delay prior fix GCC sync's aliasing on real clips? Window length (shared audio) is the lever: 97% wrong at 1 s, 38% at 2 s, 16% at 3 s on the failing clips; a tone clip needs a prior tighter than its period.
